The main takeaway from our work is that

, in contrast to the state-of-the-art, DroidSieves classification is based on the detection of obfuscated code patterns, which are not only more resilient to obfuscations than syntactic features, but also more accurate and efficient.

, by leveraging the fact that malware families are characterized by similar code structures, we can achieve high accuracy and resilience to obfuscation by focusing on the detection of such structures, instead of the detection of individual malicious features.
DroidSieve is able to achieve high classification accuracy, while being orders of magnitude faster than existing approaches, and resilient to the obfuscation techniques used by Android malware.
